assertions.name: A2_ordering_changes_the_answer
assertions.source: all-pairs swings 4.35% (3He) and 5.05% (3H) at fixed bond multiset

assertions.name: A3_strong_bond_prefers_adjacency
assertions.source: pnn > npn and pnp > ppn on the all-pairs value

description: Finds the sparse route to higher A and uses reordering at A = 3 as a cheaper discriminator than A = 4. The chain's transfer operator is exactly RANK ONE: tr(X . b . w) = tr(X) F(b,w) with F independent of the whole prefix to 2.8e-16, measured over four prefixes and three bond types (F_pn = 0.241477007350, F_nn = 0.191777066944, F_pp = 0.385581983466). So the chain telescopes, L(chain) is a sum over adjacent bonds at every A, and 4He follows with no H_12: L = 3 L_pn = 2.030464777, giving L(4He)/L(3He) = 1.50000 against B(4He)/B(3He) = 3.66618, -59%, deepening the chain's A-scaling failure. The discriminator instead comes from reordering at A = 3, which moves bond distances at fixed bond multiset: the all-pairs answer swings 4.35% (3He pnp vs ppn) and 5.05% (3H pnn vs npn), so distance genuinely matters. The strong bond wants to be adjacent, and the saturation factor is monotone decreasing in the far bond's own strength — 0.659916 (p-p), 0.650555 and 0.640829 (p-n), 0.625186 (n-n), a 5.6% spread — which is the owner's type-dependent falloff rate, measured. All-pairs is also four times less sensitive to the nucleon ordering than the chain (4.35%/5.05% against 16.02%/17.02%), a second independent argument for the all-pairs topology.
caveats: THE 'TRANSFER MATRIX' IS DEGENERATE ON THE CHAIN. The owner asked for a spectral decomposition and a decay rate within the tower; for the adjacent chain there is none to find, because the transfer operator has a single nonzero eigenvalue. That is a result, not a shortcut: it is why the chain is exactly additive and why it cannot produce any distance falloff. A genuinely non-scalar transfer operator only appears once non-adjacent bonds are present, and that is precisely the case this probe cannot yet compute at A = 4.

ALL-PAIRS AT A = 4 IS STILL NOT COMPUTED. Six bonds at distances 1,1,1,2,2,3 leave no prefix-independent F, so the telescoping fails and H_12 is unavoidable by this route. Reaching it needs a Hecke word reducer (greedy top-generator peeling with the quadratic relation, elements as {word: coefficient} maps), which is a build rather than a measurement. Nothing here extrapolates the saturation model to A = 4; the only A = 4 number reported is the exact chain value.

The ordering dependence is a MODELLING AMBIGUITY the corpus currently resolves by convention: `ordering(Z,N)` interleaves protons first, giving pnp and pnn. A physical nucleus has no preferred nucleon order, so the 16-17% chain swing and the 4-5% all-pairs swing are both artefacts of that convention. Reporting which topology minimises the artefact is the point; neither eliminates it.
